defects.evidence: AST p15 runs: text, break(line), text, ... ; read.md prints each line on its own line

defects.what: The header and footer were written as three per-section copies (hdr0-2/ftr0-2) instead of one linked part. The rendered output is correct.
defects.evidence: headers list and footers list each return 3 entries, sectionId s0/s1/s2

notes: This is a strong authoring result that meets every rubric condition. The agent's frictions point to real tool UX gaps: the trailing-backslash hard-break syntax is hard to discover for verse, create --from turned an inline [^n] into its own paragraph, and the caption did not inherit the image's --alignment. In the read view the footnote ids are in creation order (fn1, fn3, fn2), while Word numbers them 1-3, which is a small cosmetic mismatch.
weakAgentStruggle: Moderate. The agent reached a correct result but hit three dead ends. Verse newlines reflowed into prose until it found the trailing-backslash break by trial and error. An inline [^1] footnote became its own paragraph, so it fell back to footnotes add --anchor. The images add --caption paragraph needed a separate edit --alignment center. It also needed an extra edit to clear a placeholder paragraph before inserting the image.
